idiom_name: explicit per-request memoization (Hash keyed by id) over ActiveRecord's query cache
alternative: Request-scoped memoization in a repository or service (a Hash keyed by id, cleared per request) plus ActiveRecord::QueryCache in Rails, with optimistic locking (lock_version) or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE for conflicting writes; the ORM returns fresh objects per query by design, so identity is established explicitly where a workflow needs it.
implementation_notes: Rails deliberately removed the identity map - the 4.0 release notes list 'Remove IdentityMap' - and ActiveRecord today returns a new object per query, with the request-scoped query cache caching SQL results rather than guaranteeing instance identity. Prefer explicit memoization inside the service/repository that owns the workflow (a Hash keyed by id, per request) and optimistic locking for concurrent edits; hand-roll a session map only in a workflow that truly re-reads the same rows and where every load path is yours.
pitfalls: A memo stored on a shared object (class variable, constant, controller cache) leaks between requests and threads - keep it per request instance.
Memoized reads go stale after writes; drop the memo (or reload) when the same request updates the row.
Rails' query cache is request-scoped and cleared on writes - it is not an identity guarantee, so do not build identity semantics on it.
